name: level1-lose-ecology
description: Level 1 losing scenario: massive blasts with max krackle, triggering ecology score collapse and, after a sustained 150-tick zero streak, the government shutdown that actually ends the level (ECOLOGICAL_SHUTDOWN_TICKS, EcologicalDisaster.ts). depth:6 (not the originally-declared 12) throughout: the Drill panel's real click always uses its own DEFAULT_DEPTH_M regardless of what a scenario's command field declares, a new sub-class of Finding #3/#4 caught only by a real interaction-mode run (see the note on the first blast step). With the corrected, shallower/more-violent holes, ecology bottoms out at exactly 0 after just the SECOND blast (not the fifth), and the file's own original tick budget already ticks past the 150-consecutive-ticks-at-zero threshold -- the shutdown this file is named for now fires for real, no extension needed.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:5 cols:5 spacing:3 depth:6 start:5,5

expect.note: spacing:3 already matches the Drill panel's own default (DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3, Drill.ts) -- the (5,5)-(17,17) drag is a 12-unit span, round(12/3)+1=5, so the row/col/spacing part of the grid was already correct. depth was not: corrected from the originally-declared 12 to 6, the panel's own DEFAULT_DEPTH_M -- caught only by a real interaction-mode run, which failed with ecology 14.47 instead of the depth:12 command-mode trace's 48.99 (shallower holes with the same charge concentrate energy over less rock, producing far more violent fragmentation/projections). A new sub-class of Finding #3/#4: the grid tool's real defaults extend to depth, not just row/col/spacing -- every prior file's `drill_plan grid` fix only ever checked hole COUNT, which depth doesn't affect, so this class could be silently present in already-completed files too; flagged in the plan doc as a follow-up audit item.

steps.description: Charge All commits the panel's current product card / amount / stemming (ChargeStep.chargeAll, Charge.ts), and all three are reachable by click: the krackle product card ([data-action="select-explosive"][data-explosive="krackle"]) selects the explosive, 5 amount increments take 5 -> 10kg (krackle's maxChargeKg is exactly 10, so this is the top of its range) and 5 stemming decrements take 2.0 -> 1.0m. The explicit [data-step="2"] click is required because the drill step above clicks [data-step="1"] manually, which disarms autoAdvance. Amount steps by 1kg (data-field="amount", clamped to the selected product's [minChargeKg, maxChargeKg]); stemming steps by 0.2m with a 0.5m floor (data-field="stemming", Charge.ts adjustStemming). Both are plain instance fields on ChargeStep with no reset path, so they carry over from the previous charge step in the same page session — asserted before each commit rather than assumed.

Sequence's delay-step stepper carries data-field="delay-step" (Sequence.ts) for unambiguous click targeting. 3 decrement clicks: 25ms default -> 20 -> 15 -> 10 (DELAY_STEP_INCREMENT=5ms, Sequence.ts).

expect.note: confirmed via direct trace with the corrected depth:6: krackle's vibration cuts ecology from 50 to 14.47 in one blast -- deterministic (no RNG in the blast->ecology formula, ScoreManager.ts's recordVibration, called from mining.ts's blastCommand with vibrationMmS derived from result.projectionCount), safe to assert exactly in both modes.

steps.description: Product card and both steppers still hold krackle / 10kg / 1.0m from the first charge cycle in this file — ChargeStep keeps them as plain instance fields with no reset path, and a console `blast` clearing the plan does not touch them. Asserted before the commit rather than assumed, so a wrong persistence assumption fails loudly instead of quietly charging boomite at 5kg.

dstepMs is a plain instance field on SequenceStep (Sequence.ts) with no reset path -- it persists unchanged across blasts/re-drills within the same page session, so this occurrence's stepper already reads 10ms from the delay_step:10 occurrence earlier in this file. Asserted rather than assumed (Finding #75), so a wrong persistence assumption fails loudly instead of silently charging the wrong delay.

expect.note: the 2nd blast alone drives ecology all the way to exactly 0 -- not just low, the literal floor. From here applyDecay's own >0 check (ScoreManager.ts) means it can never climb back on its own without another positive contributor (a building with a positive ecology effect; this file builds nothing), so ecology now stays pinned at exactly 0 for the rest of the file, safe to assert exactly regardless of any other random event firing (confirmed via direct trace: it never moves again, including across the random event that does fire further down).
